page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS custom 64-bit ARM architecture. The server provides 48 physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture operating at 3.3 GHz. The configuration allocates one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory resources total 192 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per core. The instance includes 2850 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, with zero GPUs present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded execution and data processing throughput. In synthetic tests, the instance records top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core workloads, software compilation using Clang, and decompression tasks. Memory subsystem testing reflects strong read throughput across both cached and large uncached block sizes, reaching 187.71 GB/s on large sequential reads. The server demonstrates exceptional capacity in transactional and caching benchmarks, yielding top-tier performance in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations exceeding 136 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput also places in the top tier at 104.04 GB/s. However, language model inference displays divergent characteristics: while prompt processing on small models is fast, autoregressive text generation speed drops into lower percentiles.

The integration of 2850 GB of local NVMe storage with 48 dedicated ARM cores delivers resource density suitable for I/O-sensitive operations without requiring separate network storage volumes. Cost efficiency is driven by the power-efficient Neoverse-V3 core design, which provides predictable per-thread performance due to the absence of hyperthreading contention. Tradeoffs include architectural dependency on ARM64 binaries and modest single-core execution speed relative to its multi-core scaling. The m9gd.12xlarge is technically appropriate for distributed databases, caching clusters like Redis, build systems, web serving fleets, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring 48 dedicated physical cores running on 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V3 processors clocked at 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 192 GB of total system RAM alongside 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With no simultaneous multithreading, each vCPU maps directly to a physical core, yielding consistent multi-core throughput and strong memory bandwidth. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across software compilation, static web serving, and database transactions, alongside high Redis operations throughput. While text generation for small LLMs shows modest throughput, prompt processing and compression speeds remain competitive. This balance of dedicated ARM processing, integrated NVMe disk capacity, and high network throughput makes the instance well suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, web application tiers, and continuous integration pipelines.
